desc:
prices[i] is the price of a stock on day i. You may make as many transactions as you like; a transaction is one purchase of a single share followed by a sale on a strictly later day, and you can hold at most one share at a time.

Two rules apply: every sale costs a fee of fee (so a transaction earns sell - buy - fee), and after selling on day s you cannot buy on day s + 1. Return the maximum total profit; you are never forced to trade, so the answer is at least 0.

Example: prices = [1,4,2,8,5,9], fee = 1 gives 7: a single trade from 1 to 9 earns 8 - 1 = 7, which beats any pair of shorter trades once the fee and the rest day are paid for.
hints: Combine two familiar machines: the fee shrinks every transaction, and the rest day forbids chaining a sale straight into a purchase.
Keep three values per day: hold (own a share), sold (sold today, so tomorrow is a rest day) and free (own nothing and may buy today).
hold' = max(hold, free - p), sold' = hold + p - fee, free' = max(free, sold), all computed from yesterday's values. Answer: max(sold, free) after the last day.
editorial: The rest day rule means a share can only be bought from a state in which you did not sell yesterday. Split 'no share' into sold (a sale happened today) and free (no share and no sale today). A purchase starts from free, a sale ends in sold, and one day later sold turns into free.

Charge the fee at sale time: sold' = hold + p - fee. Initially hold = -infinity, sold = 0 and free = 0 (nothing can be sold before something is bought, and sold = 0 simply means 'no share, no trade yet').
All three updates must read the previous day's values, so compute them together. It is a single pass with three variables: O(n) time, O(1) space.
